title: Officer retires after fatally shooting 22-year-old who showed up at wrong house
description: Glenwood Earl Pysher IV, 22, was fatally shot on Aug. 23.
fullText:
A Pennsylvania police officer retired from his position after being charged with voluntary manslaughter in the fatal shooting of a 22-year-old who had arrived at a wrong house, authorities told ABC News.

Upper Pottsgrove Township Cpl. Sean Farrell, 58, voluntarily retired from his position on Wednesday, one day after he was criminally charged and suspended without pay, Upper Pottsgrove Township Manager Joseph Geib confirmed to ABC News.

The township and police department will also begin an internal review of all "relevant policies, training protocols and field responses to ensure compliance and transparency," Geib said in a statement.

Lawyer for family of college student killed by officer after arriving at wrong house wants body-cam footage

An investigation into the shooting found it was not a legal use of force by a police officer, and Farrell was charged with involuntary manslaughter, according to the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office.

Glenwood Earl Pysher IV, 22, was fatally shot by Farrell on Aug. 23 after he showed up at a house mistakenly thinking it was a friend's house.

The night of the shooting, police had responded to a 911 call for a possible attempted break-in at a residence, according to the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office.

Farrell was the first to arrive on the scene to find Pysher in the rear of the residence, according to the DA's office.

Farrell's body-worn camera captured Farrell walking down the driveway with his firearm drawn, using a mounted light for illumination. Farrell positioned himself behind a red car in the driveway when he saw a man standing on the patio, according to the DA's office.

The male, later identified as Pysher, was several feet from the rear door of the residence when Farrell yelled, "Police, let me see your hands." Then yelled, "Hands up, hands up now, drop to the ground," according to the DA's office.

Pennsylvania police officer charged in fatal shooting of student who went to wrong house

"On the video, Pysher can be seen raising his hands in the air, clearly visible, as he began walking toward Cpl. Farrell. The officer again yelled: "Drop to the ground" as Pysher continued to walk toward him with his hands raised," the DA's office said in a statement.

"Cpl. Farrell again yelled 'Drop to the ground,' then yelled 'Stop or I'll ... ' but prior to finishing that command, Cpl. Farrell fired two shots, striking Pysher twice in the chest. The victim was 17 to 20 feet away from Cpl. Farrell when he was fatally shot," the DA's office said.

Pysher was unarmed at the time of the shooting, according to the DA's office.

Pysher was out at several area bars earlier in the evening celebrating a friend's 21st birthday. The group was driven by a designated driver to the birthday celebrant's house, but Pysher left shortly after to walk a half mile to a different friend's house to continue drinking, but ended up on the back patio of the wrong house, according to the DA's office.

Farrell turned himself in to Montgomery County Detectives on Tuesday. He was assigned and his bail has been set at $75,000, according to the DA's office.

"The Township recognizes the profound grief and loss experienced by Mr. Pysher's family, loved ones, friends, and the broader community. Out of respect for the Pysher family's privacy and the integrity of the ongoing legal proceedings, Upper Pottsgrove Township and its Police Department cannot comment further on specific evidence or elements of the criminal case," Geib said.

An attorney for Farrell did not immediately respond to ABC News' request for comment. Farrell's preliminary hearing is scheduled for Sept. 10.

title: Stephen A Smith explains why he regrets voting for Harris, says her loyalty to Biden 'usurped everything else'
description: Stephen A. Smith defended his Kamala Harris vote regret on Cari Champion and Jemele Hill's podcast as the hosts accused him of targeting Black women.
fullText:
ESPN's Stephen A. Smith was repeatedly confronted over why he said he regretted voting for former Vice President Kamala Harris during a podcast released Wednesday, as hosts Cari Champion and Jemele Hill suggested he was targeting Black women.

"Flagrant and Funny" hosts Champion and Hill questioned Smith about his comments that he regretted supporting Harris in 2024 after he said it was the Democrats' plan all along to install her as the replacement for former President Joe Biden in the presidential race.

Smith referenced the widely criticized moment from ABC's "The View" on Oct. 8, 2024, when Harris appeared and said she couldn't think of anything she'd do differently than Joe Biden.

"Because when she went on 'The View' and she sat up there and said she couldn't think of anything that she would do differently, something that Sunny Hostin threw up intentionally as a softball for her to knock out the park. I'm like, when she passed up on that opportunity, this is not a dumb woman. This is a former state attorney general. This is a former senator. This is a former vice president of the United States. She is not dumb. There's only one reason she said that, because her loyalty to Joe Biden usurped everything else," Smith said.

Hunter Biden Says Kamala Harris Is Getting 'Bad Political Advice,' Refuses To Explain Loyalty Criticism

He added, "And I'm like, 'You trying to win a damn presidency? This is embarrassing. Do you want the presidency or don't you?'"

Hill suggested Harris was trying to lean into Biden's accomplishments, and said, "He accomplished a lot."

"But I understand when Sunny gave her that easy layup," Champion pressed. "But still, why was it necessary to say that you regretted voting for Kamala Harris when you knew that would take all of the hard work in which she tried to put together away from what she did?"

Smith said he supported Harris throughout the election and that he made the comments afterward.

Stephen A Smith Calls Trump An 'Upgrade' Compared To Biden Amid New York Knicks Feud

"I get where you're coming from, Cari, I really do. I think that it should have been far more upsetting if it was something that I said before the election. I did not. I supported her leading up to the election. I voted for her. I was on the airwaves talking about what it's going to take to win, win, win. And when it was over, I was honest about how I felt in the moment that that transpired," he said.

Champion accused Smith of targeting Black women specifically and said he could have made his point about his criticisms without saying he regretted voting for Harris.

Stephen A Smith Goes Off On National Black Journalists Organization After 'Personal Hit Job' Against Him

Smith countered, "Can you concede that it's a disagreement as opposed to a disparagement?"

She said she couldn't concede the point before the three turned to Smith's dispute with Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas.

America Owes Black Women 'Everything,' Rep Jasmine Crockett Rants Over July 4 Weekend

Harris's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Curtis Houck, the managing editor of the Media Research Center's NewsBusters.org, told Fox News Digital, "This level of refreshing honesty from Stephen A. Smith has sadly been in short supply for far too long. Along with ideological diversity, more commentators and journalists should be willing to admit when they're wrong or express regret. The national media demand the utmost transparency and rigorous reflection from the people they cover, so why not have it go both ways?"

Houck continued, "There's a reason why Smith is succeeding by moving outside his normal ideological bubbles. We need more of that from the ruling class, not less."

During an April interview with Sage Steele, Smith was asked about his comments prior to the 2024 election on Dave Rubin's show about voting for Harris.

"You went on his show, and you said that you voted for Kamala Harris?" Steele asked.

Steele then added, "And that you regretted it," to which Smith answered, "Yeah."

Smith went on to explain that he cast that vote because he believed Harris was capable of compromise, but said he later concluded Democrats still did not understand why they lost.

"I also believed that she was the kind of person that… could work across the aisle," Smith said. "And then when I saw how things were unfolding and how out in the clouds the Democratic Party was even after they lost the election, I just said, 'There's no hope.'"

In January 2025, Smith said during an interview with Bill Maher, "Yes, I voted for her, a lot of people voted for her, but in the end, we end up feeling like d--- fools, because we supported it. We fell for the okiedoke, as they say. If you had a primary, the likelihood is she would not have been the Democratic nominee."

Fox News' CJ Womack contributed to this report.

title: Michigan Democrat who lost Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed takes aim at Bernie Sanders over Israel stance
description: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens called Bernie Sanders part of an anti-Zionist "sickness" and questioned what he has done for Middle East peace in an interview.
fullText:
Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost last month in the Michigan Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, called out Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., in an interview over his Middle East policy, describing the progressive senator as part of an anti-Zionist "sickness."

"I really don't know what Bernie Sanders has done for peace in the Middle East, for Palestinian dignity; I can't think of anything he's totally done. It's a sickness that needs to end. You know, it's a linkage towards extremism or jihad, I don't know," she said in an interview with The Jerusalem Post.

Sanders has repeatedly called to end U.S. military aid to Israel and has been outspoken in his criticism of the Israeli government.

Former Bernie Sanders Official Accuses Senator Of Pushing Most Antisemitic Candidates 'In A Generation'

"I believe that anti-Zionism is a hate movement that has taken over in America and throughout parts of the West," Stevens said in the interview.

Sanders' office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

"I think that Israel is more than just a punching bag for some of the challenges that America is facing," Stevens said. "There is this bizarre obsession that has reached pitch level with calling out one country, one tiny country in the Middle East."

She was critical, however, of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying he has been a "problem."

Bernie Sanders Aims To Block Sale Of Bombs And Bulldozers To Israel, Accusing Us Ally Of 'Genocide'

Stevens endorsed El-Sayed shortly after she lost the primary. However, she urged the Democratic Senate candidate to cut ties with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, with whom El-Sayed has campaigned.

"It certainly makes sense to get rid of this Hasan Piker affiliation," she said during an interview with Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing" in August, also asserting that the Democratic plans for healthcare, democracy and Black-owned businesses are better than those of El-Sayed's Republican opponent Mike Rogers.

Asked whether El-Sayed had said or done anything other than winning the Democratic nomination to earn the support and assuage the concerns of groups that voted for Stevens, such as Jewish voters, Black voters or Reagan-era Democrats, Stevens pointed to her own good performance with those demographics, identifying herself as a Zionist Democrat and asserting that her party had room for all those communities.

"I came really close [to winning the primary] and I'm still a Democrat. I'm still out here talking about my views and values. I want the people who share my views and values to feel safe and to feel heard in the Democratic Party," she continued.

Qasim Rashid, a SiriusXM radio host and human rights lawyer, told Fox News Digital in a statement that Stevens' comments are "profoundly disappointing and not helpful."

"It is a well-established fact that the Israeli government has targeted and killed civilians. Leading human rights organizations and scholars, including Israeli scholars, have documented it as genocide," Rashid said.

"Our own Leahy laws in the United States require that we stop funding governments when there is credible evidence of mass human rights atrocities. By continuing to insist on arming Israel as it is violating international human rights law, Haley Stevens is on the wrong side of history.

"And she's also jeopardizing losing the state of Michigan to MAGA Republicans. This is not being thoughtful or logical. It certainly is not following the call of international human rights law and constitutional law that she took a sworn oath to uphold."

Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens Backs El-sayed After Narrow Primary Defeat, Calls Socialism 'Dangerous'

Zheng Qinwen flopped to the court then jumped up in a fist-pumping celebration Thursday after battling into the US Open third round, the 2024 Olympic gold medallist relishing the return of her game -- and her competitive fire.

The former world number four endured an injury-plagued 2025 that included a longer than anticipated recovery from elbow surgery.

She missed the Australian Open and has struggled to regain her form, and the mindset of a champion.

"Before the surgery, for me winning is like drinking water -- everything comes natural, everything comes fluent," Zheng said after beating Yulia Putintseva 6-4, 2-6, 6-1 to reach the third round.

"After my surgery, I had some tough matches against the best players in the world (and) I'm close but I don't get them.

"Now after two, three months I really felt the first time in this tournament I find myself, I found my fire back during the competition."

Zheng sank so far in the rankings that she had to go through qualifying to book her US Open berth.

She grudgingly acknowledged that grinding through the qualifiers may have helped her regain her competitive edge -- but that didn't really take the sting away.

"It takes a while for me to accept my ranking dropped to 125 and, OK, I need to actually play qualies," she said.

Now she's in the thick of the main draw and will face former Australian Open champion Keys for a place in the last 16.

Zheng is looking forward to the test -- and likely a chance to step back onto one of the main show courts of Flushing Meadows after toiling through two rounds on the outside courts.

title: Louisiana Judge Rules Players Can Go From NFL Back to College
description: The ruling allows players to go from the NFL to college rosters.
fullText:
LSU and Lane Kiffin are victorious—for now.

On Thursday evening in a courthouse in Baton Rouge, Judge William Jorden issued a ruling that extends legal protections for several football players seeking to go from the NFL preseason back to college rosters.

The ruling applies to dozens of players across multiple sports, and challenges the implementation of the NCAA's new age-based eligibility rule, rather than focusing on professional participation. It has sweeping implications, notably allowing players who have played in NFL preseason to sign with college rosters for the first time.

In the wake of the landmark decision, the most immediate question was whether some of the athletes in the case would appear in games—including Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who had signed NFL contracts but have since secured deals to play for LSU this season. LSU will have to make that choice, but has previously signalled they would roster these athletes if given the chance.

Those players are now protected by a court order.

The next question: whether the SEC and NCAA would be legally allowed to penalize LSU under the court's order. LSU is now protected, as Jorden entered a specification protecting the school from sanctions coming from the NCAA or SEC.

The case also raised an existential question: whether the SEC has the power as a conference to enforce its rules, especially in a legal environment where the NCAA is regularly sued. That last question wasn't answered by the ruling Thursday night.

The conference also filed a separate lawsuit of its own in Alabama federal court against LSU, Kiffin, and athletic director Verge Ausberry. With echoes of the Big 12's case against Texas Tech over Brendan Sorsby, the SEC is seeking a federal ruling that would ensure it could prevent LSU from playing these athletes.

The SEC is likely to continue proceedings in that case, especially if LSU rosters Harris and Wright for Saturday's game.

The landmark decision ends a contentious day in Baton Rouge, after several hours of oral arguments, including three hours of questioning for SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey, according to those present in the courtroom and reportedly left through a side door due to security concerns.

A web of elected officials either participated or looked on in person and from afar, including Louisiana attorney general Liz Murrill, who filed a brief in support of players and attended the proceedings. During the testimony, she singled out Dae'Quan Wright, saying, "Dae'Quan Wright, who played for Ole Miss, says he lost out on seven-figure NIL money in a fifth year. Mississippi didn't fight for him, but Louisiana will."

The legal battle didn't originate as one over former NFL players, however. The first Louisiana state case was one of many filed against the NCAA challenging the implementation of its new "age-based eligibility policy." The new rules allow players five seasons of eligibility—but the NCAA said it would not extend this new policy to players who started college in 2022 and had already exhausted four years of eligibility.

The players who filed the Louisiana suit were part of this group, but the case drew ire because some of the athletes had signed NFL contracts (even preseason deals) and been listed on NFL rosters. After Judge Jorden issued a temporary restraining order in favor of the players, LSU scooped up two of them: Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris.

In response, the SEC (as well as other conferences) released a policy banning players with NFL preseason experience. Neither the players nor LSU appeared to back down, however: Kiffin allowed Wright to join LSU practices earlier this week, while players' attorneys got the SEC added to the temporary restraining order.

Because of the SEC's lawsuit, the drama is likely only beginning. The case argues that the SEC would be harmed if LSU rosters players with NFL preseason experience or who signed NFL contracts, and asks a judge to "enter a preliminary and permanent injunction prohibiting Defendants from violating the Conference's First Amendment rights by compelling the Conference to associate with conduct that is contrary to the Conference's purpose and mission."

Attorneys for the SEC and/or NCAA are expected to file immediate appeals of Jorden's injunction in the hopes that it could be at least paused before Saturday.

LSU's roster for the season is due to be finalized on Friday. On Saturday, the Tigers will finally take the field against Clemson for the most highly anticipated team debut of the year.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry declared in a celebratory post on X/Twitter after the ruling: "Let's spot the ball! #GeauxTigers!"

title: After winless 2025, UMass beats power conference foe for the first time as a 29.5-point underdog against Rutgers
description: Before Thursday night, the Minutemen's last win came in October of 2024.
fullText:
UMass finally has a win over a power conference program. And it wasn't even close, either.

The Minutemen upset Rutgers 37-21 as 29.5-point underdogs on Thursday to begin the 2026 college football season. Since moving up to college football's top level in 2012, UMass had never beaten a team in one of the power conferences before it pulled off what will assuredly be one of the biggest upsets of the season on the first night of play in Week 1.

Rutgers QB Dylan Lonergan committed four turnovers. His third interception with 4:35 to go ended any chance of a miracle comeback for the Scarlet Knights, who looked like the far inferior opponent to a team that hadn't won a game since Oct. 26, 2024.

UMass QB Pop Watson threw three touchdowns in the first half. The Virginia Tech transfer is a Massachusetts native and went back to his home state after three years with the Hokies and just one TD pass over 63 attempts.

The victory is also the first for UMass coach Joe Harasymiak. He was hired to succeed Don Brown after serving as Rutgers' defensive coordinator from 2022 through 2024. The Minutemen went 0-12 in Harasymiak's first season in 2025. That season included a one-point loss to FCS-level Bryant and just a singular one-score loss to an FBS opponent.

UMass has been one of the most hapless programs in college football since moving up to the FBS level. The 1998 FCS champions have never won more than four games in a season over the past 14 years, and that's only happened twice. UMass has won two or fewer games in eight of the 13 previous full seasons and went 0-4 in 2020.

Overall, the Minutemen were just 26-134 entering Thursday night's game.

Even if UMass gets to a bowl for the first time in program history in 2026, the loss could be a harbinger of a rough season to come for Rutgers. The Scarlet Knights went 5-7 in 2025 and have games against USC, Indiana, Michigan and Penn State in Big Ten play. A second straight season without a postseason appearance is suddenly looking very, very likely. And September just started.

title: Cowboys Move Money On 3 Contracts, Create $19 Million In Salary Cap Room
description: Dallas front office bookkeeping shifts money for three key stars, arming the roster with massive flexibility for a potential blockbuster trade to bolster a 2026 title run.
fullText:
FRISCO - The Dallas Cowboys front office has done it again.

The Cowboys on Thursday made three alterations in the contracts of a trio of high-priced standouts and in doing do have created $19 million in salary-cap room.

The trio: Veteran defensive tackle Kenny Clark, cornerback DaRon Bland and tight end Jake Ferguson.

The changes, first reported by ESPN, don't change the salaries of the involved players; as is often the case, this is largely simply a bookkeeping move.

But it does push their money into future years, adding ballast to down-the-road salary caps.

Owners Jerry and Stephen Jones have in the past argued against this strategy, insisting that teams eventually "pay the piper'' when doing this.

In reality, for a team that thinks it's a contender now? It's a clever way to manipulate the cap.

Oh, and yes, it's also a way to create immediate room for a coming blockbuster acquisition ... so Cowboys fans who dream of Dallas trading for a pricy talent like Raiders pass-rusher Maxx Crosby?

This sort of move can fit that dream.

Dallas now figures to have about $33 million in cap room for 2026. As it happens, if Crosby is traded, his acquiring team would reportedly initially be on the hook for $31 million for the season, though a restructuring of that deal can be in play as well.

Per ESPN, the new cap flexibility for 2026 season means that Clark's 2027 cap number jumps up about $1.5 million, that Bland's number jumps by $2.15 million annually and that Ferguson's jumps by $1.2 million.

So even with the move, and even understanding the philosophical arguments here, that's not that much to "pay the piper'' ... especially if it helps the Cowboys contend for postseason success.

As always, it's key to remember that the players involved aren't "sacrificing'' anything; again, this is just a bookkeeping tool.

But it's an aggressive one from a Cowboys front office that is obviously planning on doing big things in 2026.

title: Somers pulls out tough 20-13 football opener win over Mamaroneck

Mamaroneck had a similar mantra last fall, and had the comeback victories to support it, during a run that captured its first Section 1 championship.

The Tigers threatened to overcome a 14-point deficit, and came awfully close, but Somers forced two fourth-quarter turnovers on downs in the red zone, including a stop with 39 seconds left that enabled them to pull out a tough 20-13 win in the teams' season opener.

Luke Balancia, Jayden Abruzese and quarterback Tristan Iglesias each rushed for a touchdown, and the Tuskers defense excelled in the clutch. Cameron Violante snagged two interceptions and had two pass breakups in the end zone, including one with 1:02 remaining to protect the one-score lead.

fullText:
Mark Sanchez agreed to plead guilty Thursday in the Indianapolis stabbing case, wiping out a jury trial that was scheduled to begin Sept. 8, according to a report by The New York Post.

The deal lands nearly 11 months after a back-alley confrontation cost Sanchez his network television job, and it leaves unanswered the question of how much prison time the former quarterback may now face.

Prosecutors and Sanchez's attorneys filed a joint motion in Marion County Superior Court 21 asking the judge to scrap the trial date and schedule a plea and sentencing hearing instead, according to NBC Sports' Charean Williams. Which charges he plans to admit has not been made public. A judge must approve and accept the plea bargain.

"This is a positive development," said Nick Sanchez Jr., legal adviser to Mark Sanchez. "We are finalizing an agreement with the prosecutor's office that provides a path toward resolving the state's case," he added, quoted by NBC Sports.

Both sides have floated Nov. 9 or 16 as sentencing dates, as reported by the Daily Mail. The trial had already been pushed back five times.

Shortly after midnight on Oct. 4, 2025, Sanchez walked into a loading area behind the Westin Hotel in downtown Indianapolis and confronted Perry Tole, a 69-year-old truck driver collecting used cooking oil on his overnight route, according to an Associated Press account. Sanchez, then 38, was in town to provide in-game analysis for the Raiders-Colts game to be broadcast by Fox the next afternoon.

Officers wrote that Sanchez smelled of alcohol and slurred his words while insisting Tole had no business parking in the alleyway area, based on charging documents obtained by USA Today. Sanchez climbed into the cab without permission, kept Tole from reaching his phone, then shoved him and slammed him to the ground.

Tole emptied pepper spray at him. Sanchez kept coming, according to the account. Tole, who later said he believed the man was trying to kill him, drove a knife into Sanchez's upper torso four times, as detailed by People magazine.

Sanchez ran, was found bleeding and went into surgery and was listed in critical condition before stabilizing. Tole was cut deeply across the face. He was never charged because investigators concluded he had defended himself.

Marion County Prosecutor Ryan Mears described the fight as a situation that "did not need to occur," per the Associated Press.

Sanchez initially faced three misdemeanor charges — battery resulting in injury, public intoxication and unlawful entry of a motor vehicle. Prosecutors added a Level 5 felony two days later — battery resulting in serious bodily injury, carrying one to six years behind bars and a $10,000 fine. Sanchez pleaded not guilty, left the hospital Oct. 12 and posted a $300 cash bond, according to a Guardian report.

Sanchez had built a second career as a broadcaster. The No. 5 overall pick in 2009, taken by the Jets, played a decade in the league and reached two AFC Championship games, then worked at ESPN and ABC after retiring in 2019 before joining Fox as a game analyst in 2021.

Brady Quinn took his seat for that Raiders-Colts broadcast. Sanchez never returned to the job. Fox confirmed on Nov. 7 that he was no longer with the network, then hired Drew Brees to work alongside Adam Amin, as detailed by The Guardian.

No broadcaster has hired him since.

Tole's civil suit remains open against Sanchez, Fox and the ownership group behind St. Elmo Steak House, according to the Indianapolis Star. Attorneys on both sides say that case is close to settling.

title: Vikings Fans Aren’t Going To Like This Caleb Banks’ Rookie Year Projection
description: Caleb Banks was always bound to be a work in progress. fullText:
Caleb Banks was always bound to be a work in progress. That's partially why many were surprised when Minnesota pulled the trigger on him with the 18th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

With him missing all of OTAs after breaking his foot at the NFL Scouting Combine, his uninspiring preseason wasn't all that surprising. His lack of conditioning, on the other hand, was a bit more alarming. He looked gassed at certain points, and some question whether he'll be in game shape once the regular season rolls around.

His pad level has also been a significant concern (which is common among players with his size). His 6'6″ height makes it easy for opposing offensive linemen to get under his pads, and he has to work extra hard to counteract that fact.

Purple Daily's Judd Zulgad gave some insight into that conversation during the team's second preseason matchup against Baltimore. "Caleb Banks needs a ton of work and now looks exhausted. Banks was used to overpowering o-linemen in college but now is easily being handled and his pad level is way too high." Zulgad wrote on X.

All things considered, he'll have some things to iron out before he's ready to make a major impact. NFL.com draft analyst Lance Zierlein doesn't think he'll show much improvement during the 2026 campaign. He thinks the towering DT will only put up 16 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, and 1 sack this season.

"Conditioning and consistency issues plague the 6-6, 327-pounder early in the season, leading to a modest snap count and sparse production." Zierlein wrote.

The league's most efficient defensive lines feature healthy rotations. However, you'd definitely like to see your first-round selection carve out a key role in that rotation. You'd want to be in a position where the coaching staff doesn't want to take him off the field, and he raises the unit's level of play when he's out there.

Unfortunately, at least early this season, that outcome appears unlikely for Banks. He's undoubtedly talented, but is also extremely raw. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores might be able to tap into his upside this season, but even the best coaches require some time to get to know a player's on-field impact.

The disparity between Banks and Domonique Orange, whom the team selected in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, will be an interesting development to follow this season.

As it stands right now, if there were a roster competition between the two of them, the battle would be a unanimous decision. And the team's first-round selection wouldn't be the one coming out on top. Unlike Banks, Orange has shown instant flashes throughout both training camp and the team's three preseason matchups.

They have vastly different skill sets, and Orange didn't show much juice in the pass-rushing department at the collegiate level. However, if Banks doesn't show that he's ready, then the presence of the Iowa State product could effectively keep him off the field on early downs.

Getting early returns from a third-round selection is usually a great thing. It wouldn't be the most promising development if it's coming at the expense of the first-round pick, though.

title: Judge makes pivotal ruling in favor of former NFL players attempting to return to college football
description: A federal judge has granted an injunction that could reshape the LSU Tigers’ roster and college football eligibility, paving the way for more than 40 athletes, including potential LSU transfers Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, to return to the college…
fullText:
The college football season got well underway Thursday night. However, the sports world was also watching closely as the SEC filed a lawsuit against LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin. The move came ahead of a critical hearing to determine whether a temporary restraining order (TRO) would remain in effect before the scheduled trial date.

A crucial decision could determine the fate of dozens of athletes looking to return to college sports. That group includes two former NFL players who are seeking to join LSU after a TRO allowed them to leave professional football and enter the transfer portal.

MORE: Bombshell report on UNC football investigation include concerning details around key staff members

Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that a federal judge has granted an injunction paving the way for the athletes to return to college football. The ruling will also likely prevent the SEC from imposing sanctions against LSU for adding former professional players to its roster.

Jan 8, 2026; Glendale, AZ, USA; Mississippi Rebels tight end Dae'Quan Wright (8) scores a touchdown against the Miami Hurricanes during the 2026 Fiesta Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

"Injunction granted by Judge William Jorden, paving the way for NCAA and SEC eligibility for more than 40 atheltes. That group includes potential LSU transfers Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, setting up a seismic decision for LSU whether they put them on the roster, which is due tomorrow." Thamel reported on X.

The SEC still has an active lawsuit against LSU and Kiffin, but Thursday's ruling could significantly weaken the conference's position. The injunction creates a major obstacle for the SEC if it attempts to punish LSU or other programs for following the court's order.

The conference has remained adamant about enforcing its rules and potentially sanctioning teams that bring former professional athletes back into college football. However, taking action against LSU could now create another legal battle if those sanctions conflict with the federal court's injunction.

MORE: SEC officially files lawsuit against LSU, Lane Kiffin in federal court

The situation also mirrors the recent chaos surrounding Texas Tech and former quarterback Brendan Sorsby. The Big 12 came close to sanctioning the Red Raiders before the legal situation surrounding player eligibility continued to evolve.

Jul 20, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey speaks to the press during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Now, the SEC faces a similar decision. The conference has shown no indication that it intends to back down from its position, but this latest ruling could force it to reconsider how aggressively it pursues sanctions.

For LSU, the immediate priority is getting its roster finalized. With the deadline approaching, the Tigers now have a path to add Wright, Harris and potentially other athletes affected by the ruling.

The broader implications could be even more significant. If the injunction remains in place, it could further reshape how college football handles athletes with professional experience and create another major challenge for the NCAA and its conferences.

fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies have gutted their farm system to remain in contention for many years.This is why it's so important to get the most out of the top prospects they do have. It hasn't been an ideal season for top positional prospect Aidan Miller, who hasn't played at all due to a back issue.However, Scott Lauber of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports the shortstop's return may be sooner than we realize.On Phillies Extra, the Inquirer's baseball podcast, minor league director Luke Murton said the 22-year-old is progressing very well.The Phillies have been vague with updates on Miller, especiallysince a June 5 spinal procedure to relieve recurring low-back pain.

While the Phillies may not have as glaring a need in the infield with the addition of second baseman Luis Arraez, it would be good to get Miller some actual reps before the impending lockout.

Those reps could be at any level in the minor leagues in the near future.

"I don't want to overpromise and underdeliver, but there may be a surprise in the near future," Murton said. "I'll say that. I'll leave it at that for now."

Murton also suggested that the Phillies have taken a slow approach with Miller, rather than rushing him back. Injuries of this kind are tricky and can flare up at any time.

"He wants to be on the field," Murton said. "It's hard. But he also understands the big picture. He's got a long career ahead of him. … Just from seeing him move around of late, he's moving as well as I've ever seen him. And so I'm excited about where he's at right now. I'm excited about where he's going to go."

The minor league season is nearing a conclusion, with Low-A and High-A wrapping up Sunday, Double-A on September 13, and Triple-A on September 20. However, the Phillies' Low-A team qualified for the playoffs next week. That could be a logical point for Miller to have a rehab assignment to get back into the swing of things.

He could also make his mark in the Arizona Fall League, beginning on October 3. He was supposed to participate in the AFL last season, but due to back issues, he had to withdraw.

The Phillies drafted Miller in the first round of the 2023 MLB Draft out of high school. He has consistently been a top-100 prospect, with his pre-2026 ranking at No. 23 per MLB Pipeline. He has fallen to No. 61 amid his absence.

In 2025, between Double-A and Triple-A, Miller slashed .264/.392/.433 with 14 home runs and 59 stolen bases.

While he is defensively best at shortstop, Miller is considered to be a future third baseman due to being blocked by Trea Turner. With Alec Bohm entering free agency after this season, this might be the most likely outcome.

While Miller likely won't make his debut until 2027 or 2028, depending on how long the lockout is, the future is bright for him, and Phillies fans should be excited about his impending return.

Editor's Note: This is the 16th installment of a Detroit Hockey Now series assessing the Detroit Red Wings' prospects' path to the NHL. The emphasis will be on what their chances are of playing regularly in the NHL and when we can expect to see them wearing the Winged Wheel.

Detroit Hockey Now Ranking: No. 16 Red Wings prospect

Age/Experience: 22, 2 AHL games.

Dylan James doesn't fit the usual NHL prospect mold. Generally, when an NHL-drafted player spends all four of his eligible seasons playing NCAA hockey, it's not a good sign of his potential as a pro prospect. In the case of James, that four-year stay was all part of the plan.

"I wanted to go back to North Dakota for my senior year," said James, selected 40th overall by the Detroit Red Wings in the 2022 NHL Entry Draft. "I mean, that place is so special.

Dylan James x2🚨🚨#LGRW pic.twitter.com/mpvN3qX5fK

"Obviously, I wanted to grow my game offensively, and I did that. So I was happy with that."

He's pleased that the Red Wings have allowed him to evolve at his own pace.

"Some teams rush their prospects just to, I guess, own their rights once they're signed," James said. "Detroit allowed me to go back my senior year. It was, I guess, a little risky on their part. But yeah, I was grateful for it."

James improved his offensive output in each of his four seasons at North Dakota. In 2025-26, his senior season, he scored a career-high 21 goals.

"A little bit of it was opportunity," James said. "I wasn't on the power play for the first three years of college. So senior year I got that power-play opportunity, and that helped me just gain confidence, even five-on-five, too.

What a thing of beauty from Dylan James! #UNDproud | #LGH pic.twitter.com/YtnfPKgsTR

"We had a new coaching staff. They were great with teaching us the offensive side of things and how to score more."

Moving to the AHL Grand Rapids Griffins following his college season, a guy known for his defense was contributing to the offense. In two AHL games, James scored two goals.

He's a stellar penalty killer. A strong skater, James uses his speed to take away time and space.

James is a physical presence on the forecheck, pressuring defensemen into committing turnovers.

Coaches can trust his game without the puck.

He has the skating ability, the defensive acumen, and the 200-foot game. The question that James will need to answer to make the show is whether he can generate enough offense to be an effective player at the NHL level.

As noted, he's already 22. In fact, James will turn 23 in October. His hockey biological clock is ticking.

If he's not knocking on the door to move up to the Red Wings by the end of his second AHL season, it doesn't bode well for James having an NHL future.

title: Donovan Mitchell Says Cavaliers Deserve The Heat After Multiple Playoff Failures
description: Donovan Mitchell admits Cavaliers earned criticism after latest failed playoff run.
fullText:
In the Eastern Conference, the New York Knicks are the team to beat. As the reigning NBA champions with a stacked roster, all eyes will be on the Orange and Blue as they attempt to become the first back-to-back title winners since the Golden State Warriors in 2018.

On paper, the Cleveland Cavaliers have all the tools they need to usurp the Knicks and make history with an NBA Finals run of their own, but critics are not sold on the idea of them going all the way after repeated playoff failures. For Cavs star Donovan Mitchell, the sentiment of doubt is understandable given his team's history of collapse when the stakes are highest.

"We got swept. We deserve the criticism that comes with that. That's warranted," said Mitchell on the 'Cousins' podcast with Tracy McGrady and Vince Carter. "We went to 2 Game 7s when we should've closed both teams out in 6. We didn't take care of business. If we had taken care of Detroit at home and not lost by 20, then we would have four days off heading into the next series, but we didn't take care of business. That's kind of where you look inward and be like, 'forget the sweep, let's talk before that. We should have handled business before that.' That's no disrespect to Toronto or Detroit, but we were in a position to win it and didn't handle our business."

Before the 2026 playoffs, the Cavaliers had won 64 games led by the combined talents of Mitchell, Darius Garland, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen. They looked like a budding dynasty in the East, only to collapse in the second round to a Pacers team that bullied them for the entire series.

That defeat set up Darius Garland's departure the following season, which brought James Harden to Cleveland as the new star point guard. He and Mitchell played well together in 2025-26 and went as far as the Conference Finals before getting absolutely obliterated. His team was swept in an embarrassing fashion by the New York Knicks, ending their season with a crushing blow that Mitchell still thinks about today.

What makes it so tough is that the Cavaliers could have helped their chances by closing out their previous series earlier. In the first two rounds, they had to fight all the way to seven games, wearing them down for their fight against the Knicks. The results were exactly what you'd expect, and Mitchell blames himself for not handling business.

Naturally, in the aftermath of so many disappointing seasons, he understands why fans have lost all faith in the Cavaliers. Even after adding Peyton Watson this summer, many are just not convinced they have what it takes to succeed under pressure, especially against teams like the Knicks, 76ers, and the Heat.

That's why Mitchell is determined to change the narrative by taking his team farther than they've been since LeBron James' departure. With averages of 27.9 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 5.7 assists per game last season, we know Mitchell has the game to lead the Cavaliers to glory, but he can't expect anyone to believe they are ready to win it all.

title: Report: Kawhi Leonard trade to Raptors remains ‘on track’ after Clippers punishment
description: The Los Angeles Clippers might be destined for NBA purgatory once their historic punishment for the Kawhi Leonard endorsement scandal begins to strip them of valuable roster-building assets. Leonard, meanwhile, appears poised to escape the situation largely unscathed. An agreed-upon trade to send Leonard from the Clippers to the Toronto Raptors remains “on track to be completed” now that the ...
fullText:
The Los Angeles Clippers might be destined for NBA purgatory once their historic punishment for the Kawhi Leonard endorsement scandal begins to strip them of valuable roster-building assets.

Leonard, meanwhile, appears poised to escape the situation largely unscathed.

An agreed-upon trade to send Leonard from the Clippers to the Toronto Raptors remains "on track to be completed" now that the NBA's investigation is complete, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

"I'm told both teams did communicate, last night, an intention to move forward," Charania said Thursday on ESPN's "Get Up."

On Wednesday, the NBA announced it was stripping the Clippers of five first-round draft picks (2029-33) and fining them $30 million for violating the league's salary cap circumvention rules, having found the team funneled money to Leonard through four endorsement deals, including one with Aspiration Partners.

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for a year for "knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities," the NBA said after completing a probe that it had opened last year following a report on "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast.

Leonard was ordered to pay $700,000 in restitution, but he was not suspended, nor was his contract voided.

And, soon, he is reportedly expected to be traded to the Raptors, who had agreed during the investigation to acquire the 35-year-old star for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and a haul of picks, including 2031 and 2033 first-rounders. The trade could not go through until the investigation concluded.

That's why ESPN insider Brian Windhorst described Leonard as an "unmitigated winner."

"He collected tens of millions of dollars in endorsement deals which are not permitted by the NBA, and he was fined $700,000 in restitution," Windhorst said on "Get Up" on Thursday. "That's the greatest investment you could ever make. It's better than a Ponzi scheme that the Aspiration guy was running, I'll tell you that."

Leonard, a two-time NBA Finals MVP, led the Raptors to a championship in 2019 during a previous, one-year stint with Toronto.

"He's very likely going to get traded to Toronto, where … he's going to get a contract extension worth tens of millions," Windhorst continued. "He's going to profit from this enormously. And my guess is, on opening night, the Toronto Raptors fans will cheer him because he won them a championship [in 2019]. He can't get on the plane to Toronto fast enough."

A seven-time All-Star, Leonard averaged 27.9 points and 6.4 rebounds per game last season.

Should the trade go through, Leonard would become the headliner on a contending Raptors team that finished as the Eastern Conference's No. 5 seed last season and employs building blocks including Scottie Barnes, R.J. Barrett and Immanuel Quickley.

The Clippers, meanwhile, would pair Ingram with point guard Darius Garland and No. 5 pick Keaton Wagler in a likely rebuild, with their draft assets set to start disappearing in 2029.

title: ‘I will not be silenced’: Enes Kanter Freedom suing WNBA team
description: Enes Kanter Freedom has filed a lawsuit against the Chicago Sky, stemming from his ejection from Wintrust Arena last month following an altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. fullText:
Enes Kanter Freedom has filed a lawsuit against the Chicago Sky, stemming from his ejection from Wintrust Arena last month following an altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Kanter Freedom announced the news Thursday afternoon on X, including a photo of the first page of his lawsuit.

"I'm taking legal action over my ejection from the @chicagosky  game while peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights," the former NBA center wrote. "My T-shirt did what the whole @WNBA apparently couldn't: define a woman. No threats. No violence. Just biology. And somehow, that required a security escort. You don't have to agree with my speech but you don't get to silence me for it. I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech."

Just filed a federal complaint.

I’m taking legal action over my ejection from the @chicagosky game while peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights.

My T-shirt did what the whole @WNBA apparently couldn’t: define a woman.

No threats. No violence.… pic.twitter.com/LqQO6x4z0X

— Enes Kanter FREEDOM (@EnesFreedom) September 3, 2026

Kanter Freedom's claim was filed in U.S. District Court and cites the Chicago Women's Basketball Operations, LLC, which runs the Sky, as a defendant, along with the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority (MPEA), which financed and built Wintrust Arena, and the City of Chicago.

In the suit, he argues that the three entities "combined and conspired" and "wrongfully ejected" him from the Aug. 23 game and subsequently permanently banned him from Wintrust Arena because of his views on gender identity and transgender athletes in women's sports.

"The Chicago Sky; MPEA, through Wintrust Arena Security; and the City of Chicago, by its Police Department, worked together to eject Plaintiff in retaliation for protected expression, and continue to work together to enforce the ongoing, unconstitutional ban of Plaintiff from Wintrust Arena, which is public property owned by MPEA," the claim reads.

Kanter Freedom sat courtside at the game wearing a shirt reading "WOMAN noun, adult human female." During the third quarter of the game, he says he stood up and celebrated a three-pointer made by Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever, who has spoken out against transgender women playing women's sports.

At that point, Kanter Freedom says Cloud "initiated a vulgar, profanity-laced verbal tirade" and "charged nearly half the length of the court" to confront him courtside.

"Plaintiff Freedom believes that Cloud's attack was motivated and triggered by the message on Plaintiff's shirt and Plaintiff's widely publicized viewpoint on protecting the integrity of women only sports," the lawsuit adds.

Kanter Freedom is asking the court to declare the defendants violated his First Amendment rights and is also seeking "an award of nominal and compensatory damages for Plaintiff's losses incurred."

title: LSU football players get massive legal win vs NCAA and SEC

Former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Smith and former Ole Miss defensive tackle Zxavian Harris each got one step closer to playing for LSU. Smith and Harris seek to return to college after spending part of the Summer with NFL franchises. Both players were undrafted in 2026 and waived by NFL teams.

Back-and-forth legal battles have allowed some players from the class of 2022 to gain a fifth year of eligibility.

The athletes are free to be rostered by schools. 

LSU has been enjoined in the case, protecting them, based on named defendants (SEC)

For now, the preliminary injunction clears the way for Wright and Harris, though LSU still has to officially add the players to the roster. Final rosters are due Friday, one day before LSU's season opener vs. Clemson.

title: Jett Lawrence To Miss SuperMotocross Playoffs for Ankle Surgery
description: Three-time SMX champ goes under the knife Sept. 9 Photo by Honda. fullText:
The reigning SuperMotocross World Champion won't defend his crown, after American Honda confirmed Jett Lawrence will sit out all three rounds of the 2026 SMX Playoffs. Lawrence will instead undergo follow-up surgery on the right ankle that has troubled him all year.

The injury dates back to last December, when Lawrence hurt the ankle in training, keeping him out of the entire AMA Supercross Championship. He returned for the opening round of the AMA Pro Motocross season and was competitive throughout the outdoor series, winning four rounds and finishing second to his brother and teammate Hunter Lawrence in the final standings. But he raced through pain the whole way. That came to a head at Ironman Raceway, where he aggravated the ankle during the opening moto of the season finale and experienced what Honda described as "a renewed level of intense pain and instability."

Lawrence is scheduled for surgery September 9, at the Steadman Clinic in Vail, Colorado. Specialists there will continue to treat him through his recovery.

"I've made the decision with my team to sit out the SMX series to get my ankle back to 100% for the longevity of my career," Lawrence said. "I suffered through the summer and did everything I could to win the outdoor championship, but my ankle hasn't felt right since the start of the season, and it's even worse now after Ironman. I want to do everything I can to get back to being me."

The absence is a significant one. Lawrence has won the SMX 450 Playoffs every year since the format's inception in 2023, taking home the $1 million prize three times. This year, Jett Lawrence would have held the fourth seed in the 450 class playoffs, behind Hunter Lawrence, Jorge Prado, and Cooper Webb. Instead, his absence will open up a spot for a rider competing in the Wild Card race.

The Honda HRC Progressive team still fields a strong lineup for the playoff opener September 12 in Columbus, Ohio. Newly crowned 450 AMA Pro Motocross Champion Hunter Lawrence carries the premier-class hopes. Jo Shimoda - the reigning 250 SMX Champion - and Chance Hymas ride in the support class.

"We're sorry that Jett won't be able to go for his fourth consecutive SMX Championship, but the entire team supports him in this decision," said Brandon Wilson, Manager of Racing & Experiential at American Honda. "He has a long career ahead of him, and we're in full support of doing what's necessary to get back as close to 100% as possible."

title: Arizona Cardinals complete full 17-man practice squad

title: The Summer of Open Weights
description: Winter 2025 was the tipping point for coding agents. Summer 2026 is shaping up to be the same for open weights - and compute supply, not model quality, is now setting the price.
fullText:
Over the winter of 2025, after the release of Opus 4.5, coding agents grew tremendously and usage exploded. I think this summer is proving itself to be a similar tipping point for open weight models.

As I argued in my margin collapse blogs (part 2 here), we're starting to see some very aggressive moves on pricing. We've seen OpenAI cut the cost of 5.6 Luna - its fast, cheapest tier - by 80%, and now Sol - its flagship - by 20%.

Meta is also offering its open model Muse Spark 1.2 for an almost-free price of $0.10/$0.20 per MTok on its contributor tier (where Meta may train on your data - standard pricing is $1.25/$4.25), with currently the cheapest API price for cache reads of $0.002 per MTok on that tier (!).

Anthropic hasn't matched this pricing yet, but the FT is leading with a story about the poor uptake of Fable 5 - Anthropic's $10/$50 frontier model, its most expensive tier - (tl;dr: it's too expensive) - headline: "Anthropic's best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive". And their Claude Developer social media account is suggesting they are still (extremely?) compute starved, wanting to make their weekly limit increases permanent but struggling for capacity:

We've now got at least five AI labs outside of OpenAI, Anthropic and Google[1] offering very good models - Z.AI, DeepSeek and Kimi - plus Meta and Grok. It's been strongly suggested that Meta is going to release their frontier models as open weights, which leaves us with four open weight models of good enough quality to drive agentic sessions.

No doubt there will be more - the Ox Alpha stealth model has been getting a lot of hype[2] - but it really indicates to me that there is a huge amount of competition for this inference.

In my eyes there are two possible scenarios that play out here:

The first one is that the gap between frontier and challenger/open weights models continues to decrease substantially - to the point where it becomes almost a commodity between these models. This is extremely bad news for labs built around proprietary models. Right now, this seems to very much be the path ahead.

However, the other scenario I wouldn't discount is a huge leap from the frontier labs, which would then expand the gap. While historically this has been what happens - open weights close the gap, then just when it looks like they are about to catch up, OpenAI/Anthropic puts a new release out which expands the gap again. This time I do feel it's different - the gap has never been this small, and I'm struggling where to see this huge jump would come from. But regardless, it's definitely possible - and with many trillions of dollars of IPO market cap riding on this - I wouldn't rule out any surprises like this.

It's important to note as well that this leap could come through token efficiency too, not just pure "intelligence". The flagship models from Anthropic and OpenAI are ~5-10x more expensive than the best open weight models per token. But, it's fair to say the open weight models tend to use quite a lot more tokens per task. So if a hypothetical future Fable 6 could achieve similar intelligence to Fable 5, but use 10x less tokens to achieve the same end goal, it'd still be a very competitive model.

I recently saw this very interesting interview with Gavin Baker, who makes the salient point that the industry has a lot of compute that was reserved for say $2/GPU-hour in 2-3 year commitments going to roll "off contract" and therefore going to be repriced.

Given current rates for Blackwell GPUs are significantly above that, he makes the point that these people are hoping to pay $4/GPU-hour - the win would be a doubling of underlying costs.

I think this really makes the token efficiency angle even stronger. There is enormous competitive advantage - more so than pure intelligence I think right now - in being able to serve these models more efficiently.

Winter 2025 was about agents needing frontier intelligence at any price. This summer is about good enough intelligence at a tenth of the price - and whether the frontier labs can keep charging a premium for being slightly better.

Right now the pricing power isn't with the smartest model, it's with whoever has the megawatts to spare. OpenAI can afford to cut Luna 80% and put Sol on a three-month 20% promo because it has the capacity and the efficiency gains to back it up. Anthropic - renting 300MW from SpaceX at $1.25bn a month precisely because it doesn't - has to extend limits with a caveat that "capacity may be tight".

That flips the usual tech story. For decades software captured the margin and hardware was the commodity. Here the hardware is the margin, as I argued in xAI's new rental business. The handful of open-weight hosts - Fireworks, Together, Cloudflare and a dozen others - all have the same incentive: squeeze more tokens per GPU, because whoever does wins the price war regardless of who trained the model.

If that efficiency race keeps going, then cheap inference keeps pulling demand forward. The frontier labs' two escape routes are the ones I laid out in the margin collapse series: stay meaningfully ahead on intelligence, or make the model so much more token-efficient that the sticker price stops mattering. Fable 5 being called "too expensive" at $10/$50 tells you neither is guaranteed.

I wouldn't bet against a surprise leap - we've seen the gap close and re-widen before, and trillions in IPO market cap is a strong motivator. But this is the first summer where the open weights are close enough that most agentic work just doesn't need the frontier. That's a genuine tipping point, just like agents were last winter.

Though I do question Google's addition to this list, given their very obvious troubles (what's going on with Gemini) at the frontier ↩︎

It looks like this is another GLM model, but if not it could be another significant challenger in the market ↩︎
